action_label_encoding: labels '1'-'5' = GameAction.ACTION1-5 (1=up,2=down,3=left,4=right,5=noop); '6:x:y' = ACTION6 click at frame coords (x=col,y=row); 'C:1' = the banked L1 prefix dynamic click via experiment_4340's _apply_ka59_label (only used inside the 11-action verified prefix)
novel_mechanics_found: ka59 is a sokoban-with-ballistics: clicking an e-framed block selects it (ACTION6, costs a turn); moves are 3px steps; pressing into an adjacent object LAUNCHES that object in a 15px (5-step) flight while the pusher stays put. Three flight rules discovered: (1) WALL-EXTENSION - if the 15px landing overlaps an f-wall/void, the flight continues 3px at a time until fully clear (this is how objects cross walls, incl. a 6-row-thick wall crossed with a 21px flight); (2) BACKTRACK-CLAMP - if the flight can never become legal (would exit the arena), it clamps BACK toward the pusher to the last legal position - L4 is designed around this: the third consecutive up-push of the plus-cross overshoots past the room ceiling and clamps to rest EXACTLY in the plus-shaped target (rows 8-16); (3) CHAIN-SHOVE - any object overlapping the flying object final rest position gets displaced minimally in the flight direction (a static block sitting in the landing footprint does NOT extend the flight; it gets shoved out of the way). Also: color-11 plus-crosses are pushable but NOT selectable/clickable; targets are hollow 4-colored outlines whose INTERIOR dimensions exactly match each movable object outer dimensions (shape-matching tells you the assignment); outline borders are decorative (objects pass over and rest on them); level completes when the last object is placed. L5 (unsolved) introduced a NEW mechanic: a vertical channel holds a 6-row two-color (c=12/d=13) stack whose c/d boundary CYCLES BY ITSELF one row per action (period ~6), a 3-cell legend beside a 3x3 target box gives a mod-3 phase readout, and pushing the stack launches ALL 6 rows with the composition FROZEN at the strike phase - it is a timing/rhythm extraction puzzle.
gotchas: Selection: only e-framed (color 14) blocks are clickable; click their center pixel in frame coords. Clicking a cross does nothing but still consumes a turn.
Selected block shows a 0 (black) center; previously-selected shows 4; never-selected shows 5. Adjacent-to-pushable blocks display a black arrow on the contact side.
Pusher NEVER moves during a push; the pushed object flies. Plan pusher parking spots accordingly.
Chain-shove trap (cost me the first L4 attempt): parking a block in a flight landing footprint does NOT stop/extend the flight - the block gets shoved. Do not use blocks as flight-stoppers.

L4 room topology is one-way: the bottom room can only be exited via pushes; a lone block that descends is stranded there forever. The winning line needs only ONE block below (it ends in the bottom-room target).

L4 winning line (from fresh level): use E5 to push D0 down at cols 17-19? NO - reverse: the line that worked: D0 down via E5 push, D0 right-pushes cross to col 39 in bottom room, D0 up-pushes cross (wall-extension lands center row 33), E5 up-pushes (lands center row 18), E5 up-pushes again (backtrack-clamp seats cross in plus target center row 12), then place D0 (bottom square) and E5 (middle square).
Step HUD (bottom row): one pixel darkens per TWO actions, so ~128 actions per level, refills on level-up. Blocked moves and ACTION5 appear not to consume a tick.
ACTION5 is a no-op in this game (tested, zero frame change).
Blocked ordinary moves (into walls/room edges) are safe no-ops.

The 11-action L1 prefix from the registry replays deterministically; the whole 201-action L1-L4 line replayed identically through the reproduction gate on the first try - the game appears fully deterministic.

L5 (open frontier): stack phase advances on EVERY action including sideways moves and clicks - you cannot wait without advancing phase. Phase at strike freezes the extracted composition. The extracted 6-row stack flies over the big f-ceiling (rows 9-20) and lands at rows 3-8. Win condition not yet determined; the 3x3 box (interior rows 27-29, cols 48-50) + its d/c legend presumably specifies the required delivery.
Practical: drive the env from a persistent Python REPL and diff frames after every action; the per-action diffs make the physics obvious.
narrative: Started from the banked 11-action L1 prefix (replayed, confirmed level 1). Read the L2 board as a shape-matching sokoban (4 e-blocks vs 4 outline targets whose interiors match block dimensions exactly), discovered the 15px push-flight mechanic, and solved L2 in 49 actions on the first plan. L3 (two color-11 plus-crosses into plus-outline targets) fell to the same physics plus the discovery that crosses are pushable-but-not-selectable - solved in 45 actions, again first try. L4 required three NEW physics discoveries: chain-shove (my flight-stopper plan failed - the obstacle block got displaced instead of stopping the flight, stranding my pusher in a one-way bottom room), the 2-actions-per-HUD-pixel budget (~128/level, which un-doomed the level after I thought the HUD was spent), and backtrack-clamp (a push whose flight would exit the arena clamps back to the last legal spot - the level is DESIGNED around this: the final up-push overshoots and clamps the cross exactly into its target). Solved L4 and ran the mandatory reproduction gate on the full 201-action from-reset sequence: reached_level=4, reproduced=True. Spent the tail budget characterizing L5: a genuinely novel timing/extraction mechanic (self-cycling two-color stack, phase-frozen extraction, mod-3 legend readout). Stopped there: remaining budget (~78 steps) could not both crack the L5 win condition and gate-verify it, so I banked the verified +3 levels and documented L5 for the next attempt.
